subject: Linguistics
title: Kinship Terms
description: A quick, practical guide to Kinship Terms.

hook.text: English has one word for 'uncle.' Turkish has four—distinguishing mother's side from father's side.

buildup.text: Kinship terms vary wildly across languages, reflecting different family structures and social norms.

discovery.text: Hawaiian kinship uses the same term for mother and mother's sister—grouping by generation.

twist.text: These differences aren't just labels—they influence social obligations and family dynamics.

climax.text: Kinship systems show how deeply language and culture are intertwined in shaping meaning.

punchline.text: Who counts as 'family' depends on what your language calls them.

quiz.question: What does Hawaiian kinship terminology group by?
